versions.content: Definition of Product Line Model A Product Line Model is similar to a Product Model , but contains variation points of all binding times. A Product Model is created out of a Product Line Model by keeping certain variations, and discarding others (i.e., binding). The only variation points that are still allowed in a Product Model are PostBuild variation points. In the context of feature modeling, this selection process is steered by a Feature Selection (more precisely, the variant selection Process (binding) is controlled by variant selectors ( SwSystemconst ) who's values in turn may be derived from Feature selection). In AUTOSAR, A Product Line Model is a collection of M1 artifacts which describe a set of Product Models with common characteristics. A Product Line Model is an instance of an extended metamodel as defined in the chapter on variant handling in the Generic Structure Template [1].
